elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “either party’s liability” using the same cap.

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap includes fees paid or payable.
elements.evidence: The cap uses “the total amount paid or payable by Corio.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb measures the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause measures the 12 months preceding “the event giving rise to the liability,” not the claim. This can exclude fees accruing between the event and the claim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the applicable 12-month fee amount and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly uses the greater of the 12-month paid-or-payable amount and US$1,000,000.

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Neither party may recover indirect damages from the other, subject to the stated Section 8 exception.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Neither party may recover consequential damages from the other, subject to the stated Section 8 exception.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breaches of confidentiality obligations under Section 10 or the related NDA are defined as Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Data protection obligations are not expressly included in Excluded Claims. The content of Section 8 is not provided, so its cross-reference cannot establish this carve-out.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Security obligations are not expressly included in Excluded Claims. The content of Section 8 is not provided, so its cross-reference cannot establish this carve-out.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party’s indemnification obligations are expressly included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is expressly included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is expressly included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for infringement of the other party’s intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party’s infringement of the other party’s intellectual property rights is expressly included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Customer’s payment obligations are not subject to the liability cap as damages.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Corio’s obligation to pay fees due under the agreement is not subject to the limitation.

elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “either party’s liability” using the same cap.

elements.element: The cap is 12 months’ fees without an additional monetary floor.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of 12 months’ paid-or-payable fees and US$1,000,000, rather than a straight 12-month fee cap.

elements.element: Indemnification obligations are uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations are included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breaches of confidentiality obligations under Section 10 or the related NDA are included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

elements.element: Liability for gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is included in Excluded Claims and excepted from the cap.

result.reason: The redline does not satisfy the preferred position because it omits express uncapped carve-outs for data protection and security and changes the fee lookback trigger from the claim to the earlier event giving rise to liability. It does not satisfy the fallback because the US$1,000,000 floor remains, so the cap is not a straight 12-month fee cap. The trigger change was unnecessary and may materially reduce the cap, so the redline is neither minimal nor fully intent-preserving. Drafting is otherwise generally clear, though the second damages exclusion continues to use only the Section 8 exception rather than the newly defined Excluded Claims.
